answer.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and onboarding/signup simplification is the one direction supported by two independently consolidated records (memory_86 on shortened onboarding, memory_31 on cutting signup fields) rather than a single readout. That convergence is why I lean there over the competitor-driven instinct to discount. I want memory_73 pulled precisely because it is the memory that would justify promotional_pricing and it carries an explicit self-flagged defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact of cohort mixing rather than a real price effect. If the archive shows the lift survives cohort separation, promotional_pricing becomes a live contender against the competitor's entry pricing; if it does not, I can stop treating that memory as decision-grade. I also want memory_86 verified even though it supports my intended action, because I should check what it actually measured: it reports completion rates, time-to-value, and 'early product adoption,' all of which are upstream proxies, not qualified revenue. Two important cautions I am carrying forward rather than resolving. First, an explicit downstream value risk: memory_31 achieved its lift by removing required signup fields, and memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted demo path. Fewer captured fields can mean worse routing and lead qualification, so a first-week activation gain could coexist with flat or degraded qualified revenue. I will instrument downstream qualified-pipeline and 30/60-day retention as guardrails, not just completion rate. Second, all six memories are inherited summaries of archived experiments run on a pre-competitor market; the competitive entry is a genuine regime change, so prior effect sizes should be treated as directional priors, not forecasts. This also does not address the SMB accounts actively being lost to price, which remains an unresolved exposure that one experiment slot cannot cover. Standard experiment scale with downstream guardrails, since the direction is well supported but the revenue link is unproven.
